newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil prices deflated as futures rally flops.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil prices deflated as futures rally flops.

text.p: NWE gas oil ended Tuesday lower as benchmark IPE futures, which had shot to five-year highs over the latest Iraqi crisis, lost some gains to profit-taking.
Despite the late dip, traders said concerns over low stocks in both Europe and the U.S. as winter in the Northern hemisphere approaches would keep the market strong.
Cargoes were active despite high futures. "People were sitting waiting for futures to fall back but instead they've saw them passing the $200 mark. They're not sitting back anymore," one trader said.
French refiners bid for low sulphur at Oct IPE +$16/+$17, cif NWE. A 0.05 pct cargo sold at Oct IPE +$19, cif Bordeaux.

Some sellers said they held onto low sulphur cargoes on the expectation premiums would strengthen further. "Low sulphur looks a little tight. We're seeing demand for four to five cargoes," one seller said.

German heating oil also remained strong. End-user demand appeared to be picking up as consumers accepted prices were unlikely to return to the low levels seen in June. Premiums were assessed at Oct +$5.0/+$5.50, cif Hamburg.
